_comment: Copy this file to config.json and fill in your API keys. Use ${ENV_VAR} syntax to reference environment variables, or embed keys directly.

openrouter._comment: Use OpenRouter to access Claude and other non-OpenAI models (the Anthropic API is not OpenAI-compatible).

paper._comment: venue = paper fills obey cached exchangeInfo rules (step size, min notional), so paper rejects what Binance rejects. simple = legacy 1-decimal rule. Refresh the cache with: uv run python -m arena.instruments --refresh

live._comment: Nothing here is used while trading.mode is 'paper'. Setting mode to 'live' requires accounts, agent_accounts and allow_symbols, and fails at startup otherwise. Keep dry_run true until you have watched a full session in the journal. Secrets: use ${ENV_VAR} references, never literals.

fees._comment: Taker fee in basis points (1 bps = 0.01%). 60 = Coinbase Advanced Trade base tier. Set to 10 for Binance global VIP 0, or 0 to disable. perp_taker_bps applies to *-PERP products only (5 = Binance USDⓈ-M VIP 0); run `uv run python -m exchanges.binance_perp` to stream those contracts.

churn._comment: Turnover guard, wired into every fill path (paper and live). max_fills_per_hour counts every fill, exits included, because each one pays the taker fee. cooldown_seconds blocks re-opening the same product right after a fill. max_fee_burn_pct_per_hour is the hourly fee budget as a share of equity (0.25 = 25 bps/hour), scaled so a deposit raises it. Reducing a position is never blocked. null disables any one limit; these three come from an incident where 140 fills in two hours cost $2.06 of fees on $100 of equity to earn $0.10 gross.

exit_floor._comment: No-scratch-exit gate. A close is allowed at or beyond min_profit_bps of profit, at or beyond -stop_bps of loss (cutting a loss is never refused), or after max_hold_seconds so a stale position cannot be trapped. Anything in between pays the round trip to end up where the position started. Calibrate the band to the cost: EV is p*TP-(1-p)*SL-C, and a driftless random walk has p=SL/(TP+SL), so the band only pays if the strategy's hit rate beats that — a 50/25 band needs ~15 points of edge at a 10 bps round trip, 100/50 needs ~7. null on either bound disables the band; max_hold_seconds: null removes the timeout. enabled: false leaves exits unguarded.
